title: Leaving the Hard Bar Unplayed
story: Elena practised the difficult passage until her hands knew the notes, then stopped midway and marked the page. The others wanted a full run before the visitor arrived. She argued that a clean performance would hide the bar where the rhythm still slipped. They would hear success and remember the wrong shape. Leaving the passage unfinished forced the next rehearsal to begin at the weak point, not at the opening where everyone felt safe. The visitor could wait a week. The group grumbled. A habit of skipping the hard bar, she said, would outlast any single performance.

vocabulary.definition: A section of a piece of music
The pattern of beats in the music
A practice session before a performance

quiz.question: At what point did Elena stop playing?
options: Midway through the difficult passage
After the visitor had left the room
On the final bar of the whole piece
Before her hands knew any notes
quiz.explanation: She stopped midway through the passage.
quiz.supportingSentence: Elena practised the difficult passage until her hands knew the notes, then stopped midway and marked the page.

quiz.question: What did the rest of the group hope to do that day?
options: Play the whole piece before the visitor came
Cancel practice until the next month
Rewrite the hard bar in a new key
Ask the visitor to lead them
quiz.correctAnswer: Play the whole piece before the visitor came
quiz.explanation: The others wanted a full run before the visitor arrived.
quiz.supportingSentence: The others wanted a full run before the visitor arrived.

quiz.question: What false memory would a clean full run plant?
options: That the weak bar was already secure
That the visitor had joined the group
That the pencil marks could not be read
That practice should move to another room
quiz.correctAnswer: That the weak bar was already secure
quiz.explanation: They would hear success and remember the wrong shape of the weak bar.
quiz.supportingSentence: They would hear success and remember the wrong shape.

quiz.question: What does slipped say about the rhythm?
options: It was not yet steady
The visitor had chosen it
It belonged to a different piece
It was louder than the other bars
quiz.explanation: Slipped means the rhythm was still failing to hold steady.
quiz.supportingSentence: She argued that a clean performance would hide the bar where the rhythm still slipped.

quiz.question: Why include the remark that a habit would outlast a performance?
options: To show she is protecting later practice, not this visit
To prove the visitor cancelled the concert
To explain how the music was printed
To suggest the group should split up
quiz.correctAnswer: To show she is protecting later practice, not this visit
quiz.explanation: The remark shifts the decision from one performance to a habit that would last.
quiz.supportingSentence: A habit of skipping the hard bar, she said, would outlast any single performance.
